candidates.source_name: CBCG — Regulativa (regulatory framework hub, ME)
candidates.why_relevant: Top-level hub of the CBCG legal corpus, branching into Ustav, Zakoni, Statut and Podzakonski akti. Single best entry point to enumerate every legally binding instrument the regulator issues or applies.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Recursive HTML crawl of the four child sections; treat as the seed for a link frontier over cbcg.me/me/o-nama/regulativa/*
queries_used: Centralna banka Crne Gore odluke propisi supervizija banaka

candidates.source_name: CBCG — Podzakonski akti (bylaws / Odluke, all categories)
candidates.why_relevant: The operative body of CBCG secondary legislation, organised into seven tracked categories: monetarni instrumenti, finansijska stabilnost, kontrola banaka, kontrola pruzalaca finansijskih usluga, zastita korisnika potrosackih kredita, platni promet i platni sistemi, sanacija kreditnih institucija. Each Odluka carries its Sluzbeni list citation, which gives an exact promulgation date and therefore a compliance-deadline anchor.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Scheduled diff-crawl of each category page; capture Odluka title + 'Sl. list CG br. XX/YY' citation + linked PDF; hash PDFs to detect amendments
queries_used: Centralna banka Crne Gore odluke propisi supervizija banaka
Centralna banka Crne Gore podzakonski akti platni promet

candidates.source_name: CBCG — Podzakonski akti: Kontrola banaka (bank supervision bylaws)
candidates.why_relevant: Densest prudential sub-corpus: capital adequacy, minimum risk-management standards, key-function/business-line criteria, reporting content and deadlines, AML/CFT risk-system guidelines. Observed instruments include Odluka o minimalnim standardima za upravljanje rizicima u kreditnim institucijama (Sl. list CG 134/21) and Odluka o sadrzaju, rokovima i nacinu sacinjavanja i dostavljanja finansijskih izvjestaja banaka (34/22) — the latter is literally a deadline schedule.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: HTML+PDF harvest; extract 'rok', 'primjenjuje se od', 'stupa na snagu' phrases for deadline extraction
queries_used: Centralna banka Crne Gore odluke propisi supervizija banaka

candidates.source_name: CBCG — Regulations (English mirror of the bylaw corpus)
candidates.why_relevant: English-language mirror of the same seven regulation categories (Monetary Instruments, Financial Stability, Banking Supervision, Resolution of Credit Institutions, Supervision of Financial Service Providers, Protection of Consumer Loan Beneficiaries, Payment Operations and Payment Systems). Useful for cross-lingual term alignment and for consumers who cannot read Montenegrin, but is typically less complete/lagging versus the ME tree — always reconcile against ME.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Parallel crawl of /en/ tree; align ME/EN pairs by Sluzbeni list citation to build a bilingual glossary
queries_used: Central Bank of Montenegro regulations decisions supervision banks site:cbcg.me

candidates.source_name: CBCG — Zakoni (laws administered/drafted by the central bank)
candidates.why_relevant: Consolidated set of the primary statutes the CBCG applies — Zakon o Centralnoj banci, Zakon o kreditnim institucijama, Zakon o platnom prometu, Zakon o sanaciji kreditnih institucija, Zakon o sprjecavanju pranja novca. Statutory change is the upstream driver of every downstream Odluka and compliance deadline.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Periodic crawl; watch for consolidated-text ('preciscen tekst') republications as an amendment signal
queries_used: Centralna banka Crne Gore odluke propisi supervizija banaka

candidates.source_name: CBCG — Saopstenja (press releases, incl. Savjet CBCG session outcomes)
candidates.why_relevant: The earliest public signal for regulatory change: the Savjet CBCG (Council) adopts drafts and decisions at numbered sessions and each is announced here, typically weeks before Sluzbeni list publication. Observed examples: 'Savjet CBCG utvrdio nacrte zakona i odluke ... jacanja efikasnosti platnog sistema' and countercyclical buffer raised to 1% applicable from 1 January 2026 — a dated compliance deadline surfaced only via a press release.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Daily/weekly incremental crawl of the listing with ?id= item pagination; NLP-flag 'utvrdio nacrt', 'usvojena odluka', 'primjenjuje se od', 'sjednica Savjeta'
queries_used: "Savjet CBCG" sjednica odluke saopstenje cbcg.me
cbcg.me "javna rasprava" nacrt odluke Centralna banka Crne Gore

candidates.source_name: CBCG — Kontrolna funkcija (supervisory function hub)
candidates.why_relevant: Hub for the supervisory perimeter: bankarski sistem, registar banaka, banks in bankruptcy, financial reports of banks, supervised non-bank providers (leasing, faktoring, otkup potrazivanja, mikrokreditne finansijske institucije, kreditno-garantni fond), recognised rating agencies, restriktivne mjere, AQR, and cooperation agreements. Defines who is licensed and therefore who is in scope for every deadline.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Crawl child pages; snapshot registers on a monthly cadence to diff entrants/exits
queries_used: Centralna banka Crne Gore odluke propisi supervizija banaka

candidates.source_name: CBCG — Registar banaka (register of licensed banks)
candidates.why_relevant: Authoritative licensing register for credit institutions. Diffs against it are the cleanest evidence of licence grants, withdrawals, mergers and market entry/exit.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Monthly snapshot + row-level diff; store entity name, licence number, licence date
queries_used: cbcg.me registri platne institucije institucije za elektronski novac registar

candidates.source_name: CBCG — Registri platnog prometa (payment systems / payment institutions / e-money institutions)
candidates.why_relevant: Statutory registers maintained under the Zakon o platnom prometu: registar platnih sistema, registar platnih institucija i njihovih agenata, registar institucija za elektronski novac i njihovih agenata, plus the list of institutions whose authorisation was revoked. This is the licensing ground truth for the payments sector and directly serves the payments half of the run scope.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Monthly snapshot of all four child registers with row-level diffing; the 'oduzeto odobrenje' list is an early distress/enforcement indicator
queries_used: cbcg.me registri platne institucije institucije za elektronski novac registar
CBCG licensing payment institutions e-money register

candidates.source_name: CBCG — Platni promet (payment system function hub)
candidates.why_relevant: Operational hub for the national payment system: RTGS and DNS systems, instant payments (TIPS clone), CBCG tariff, payment-institution/e-money financial reports, consumer payment-account fees, basic payment account, payment statistics, Centralni registar transakcionih racuna, prinudna naplata. Instant-payments and TIPS onboarding are live compliance-deadline generators for Montenegrin PSPs.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Crawl the subtree; watch the instant-payments and tariff pages for dated go-live/fee-change milestones
queries_used: Centralna banka Crne Gore podzakonski akti platni promet

candidates.source_name: CBCG — Sanacija kreditnih institucija (resolution authority function)
candidates.why_relevant: CBCG acts as the national resolution authority: resolution objectives and instruments, the sanacioni fond and its contributions, and MREL requirements. MREL calibration and contribution calls are hard-dated obligations on every bank and a distinct regulatory workstream from prudential supervision.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Crawl subtree; cross-link to the 'sanacija kreditnih institucija' bylaw category under podzakonski akti
queries_used: Centralna banka Crne Gore odluke propisi supervizija banaka

candidates.source_name: CBCG — Nadzor u oblasti sprjecavanja pranja novca i finansiranja terorizma (AML/CFT supervision)
candidates.why_relevant: AML/CFT supervisory channel including the CBCG's regulatory role, guidelines for risk analysis and for establishing ML/TF risk-management systems (e.g. Sl. list CG 55/24), and supervisory expectations for obliged entities. AML is Montenegro's most active EU-accession-driven compliance area and a frequent source of new obligations and deadlines.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Crawl subtree + EN counterpart /en/core-functions/supervision-of-compliance-and-protection-of-rights/...; capture smjernice PDFs
queries_used: Central Bank of Montenegro regulations decisions supervision banks site:cbcg.me

candidates.source_name: CBCG — Zastita prava klijenata kreditnih institucija i korisnika finansijskih usluga
candidates.why_relevant: Conduct-supervision channel plus registers of credit intermediaries and housing-loan mediators; pairs with the 'zastita korisnika potrosackih kredita' bylaw category (effective interest rate, creditworthiness assessment, intermediary registration). Conduct rules bind directly on bank and PSP product operations.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Crawl subtree; snapshot intermediary registers monthly
queries_used: Centralna banka Crne Gore odluke propisi supervizija banaka

candidates.source_name: CBCG — Finansijska stabilnost / makroprudencijalne mjere
candidates.why_relevant: Macroprudential policy channel: countercyclical capital buffer, systemic risk buffer, borrower-based measures on household lending, and payment-system oversight. Buffer decisions carry explicit forward application dates (e.g. CCyB 1% applicable 1 January 2026; borrower-based measures extended to 1 January 2026), which are exactly the deadline objects this workstream tracks.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Crawl subtree + join to the 'finansijska stabilnost' bylaw category and to Savjet press releases for the announcement-to-application lag
queries_used: "Savjet CBCG" sjednica odluke saopstenje cbcg.me

candidates.source_name: CBCG — Publikacije / redovne publikacije (supervision and stability reporting)
candidates.why_relevant: Scheduled institutional reporting: Izvjestaj o radu CBCG, Izvjestaj guvernerke o sprovodjenju politike, Izvjestaj o stabilnosti finansijskog sistema, Makroprudencijalna analiza i politika, Bilten CBCG, macroeconomic reports and the bank credit-activity survey. These narrate supervisory priorities (e.g. SREP alignment with ECB methodology) and pre-announce forthcoming regulatory work.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Calendar-driven PDF fetch per publication series; index by publication date and extract the forward-work-programme sections
queries_used: Centralna banka Crne Gore odluke propisi supervizija banaka

candidates.source_name: CBCG — Politika CBCG i Strateski plan (annual policy and multi-year strategy)
candidates.why_relevant: The annual Politika CBCG and the Strateski plan CBCG 2025-2028 state, ex ante, which regulations the bank intends to draft in the coming period (EU-integration alignment, ECB SREP methodology adoption). Best single forward-looking indicator of the regulatory pipeline before any draft exists.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Annual PDF capture (ME + EN); diff year-over-year to detect newly added regulatory intentions
candidates.discovered_via_method: search snippet + snowball from Savjet press releases
queries_used: Central Bank of Montenegro regulations decisions supervision banks site:cbcg.me
"Savjet CBCG" sjednica odluke saopstenje cbcg.me

candidates.source_name: CBCG — Pristup informacijama / javni registri i javne evidencije (FOI channel)
candidates.why_relevant: Free-access-to-information channel with the Vodic za slobodan pristup informacijama and an enumerated inventory of the public registers and evidencije the CBCG holds. The inventory page is itself a pointer that reveals datasets not linked from the main navigation, and the FOI route is the legitimate escalation path for supervisory material that is not proactively published.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: One-off crawl of the register inventory to expand the URL frontier; use formal SPI request only where a dataset is confirmed to exist but is unpublished
queries_used: cbcg.me registri platne institucije institucije za elektronski novac registar

candidates.source_name: CBCG — Elektronski servisi (e-service portals)
candidates.why_relevant: Index of six CBCG digital service platforms (auctions, resident reporting, enforcement/prinudna naplata systems, transaction-account registry lookups). Each portal is a separate host/application whose terms of use and technical access model must be assessed independently before any collection.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Enumerate portal hosts, then per-portal legal/ToS review before any automated querying; several are lookup forms rather than crawlable pages
queries_used: Centralna banka Crne Gore odluke propisi supervizija banaka

candidates.source_name: Sluzbeni list Crne Gore (Official Gazette of Montenegro)
candidates.why_relevant: The legally authoritative promulgation venue for every CBCG Odluka and every law the CBCG applies. The 'Sl. list CG br. XX/YY' citation stamped on each bylaw resolves here, giving the canonical text and the exact publication date from which stupanje na snagu and compliance deadlines are computed. Adjacent to the CBCG cell but indispensable to it.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Issue-level monitoring; resolve CBCG citations to gazette documents via the pregled-dokumenta lookup. Verify whether full-text search requires subscription before designing a crawler.
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language search on the citation format seen in CBCG bylaws
queries_used: Sluzbeni list Crne Gore pretraga propisa sluzbenilist.me odluka Centralne banke

candidates.source_name: eUprava Crne Gore — e-participacija / javne rasprave
candidates.why_relevant: Montenegro's statutory public-consultation portal. Critically, CBCG-drafted primary legislation is consulted here by the Ministarstvo finansija, not on cbcg.me: the Nacrt zakona o izmjenama i dopunama Zakona o kreditnim institucijama (crypto-asset scope, ownership-stake rules, management accountability, ESG in banking supervision) ran a 20-day consultation via the ministry site and eUprava. Consultation windows carry an explicit rok za dostavljanje komentara.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Poll the Javna_Rasprava listing on a short cadence, filter for finance/banking/payments keywords, capture opening date and rok; also collect the closing 'Izvjestaj o obavljenom konsultovanju zainteresovane javnosti'
candidates.discovered_via_method: consultation query + snowball from trade-press coverage
queries_used: eUprava Crna Gora e-participacija javne rasprave Ministarstvo finansija zakon o kreditnim institucijama nacrt
CBCG javne konsultacije nacrt odluke rok za dostavljanje komentara

candidates.source_name: Ministarstvo finansija Crne Gore (gov.me) — financial-sector legislative pipeline
candidates.why_relevant: The ministry is the formal proposer of CBCG-drafted banking and payments statutes and runs their public consultations, publishes the nacrt text, the obrazlozenje and the post-consultation report. Confirmed in this run for the Zakon o kreditnim institucijama amendments and the Zakon o finansijskim konglomeratima amendments. Any CBCG regulatory watch that monitors only cbcg.me will miss the primary-law stage entirely.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Crawl the ministry news/consultation listings; wapi.gov.me/download/{uuid} serves the attached documents
queries_used: eUprava Crna Gora e-participacija javne rasprave Ministarstvo finansija zakon o kreditnim institucijama nacrt

candidates.source_name: Skupstina Crne Gore — zakoni.skupstina.me (parliamentary legislative tracker)
candidates.why_relevant: Terminal stage of the pipeline: predlog zakona texts, amendments, committee materials and adoption dates for banking and payments statutes. Gives the definitive adoption date from which CBCG must issue implementing Odluke, and typically the transposition/implementation deadlines written into the prelazne i zavrsne odredbe.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Track bill dossiers by title keyword (kreditn*, platni promet, sanacij*, pranje novca); harvest the linked PDF dossier documents
queries_used: eUprava Crna Gora e-participacija javne rasprave Ministarstvo finansija zakon o kreditnim institucijama nacrt

candidates.source_name: PropisiNet.me — consolidated Montenegrin legislation database
candidates.why_relevant: Commercial legal aggregator that publishes per-issue tables of contents of the Sluzbeni list and maintains consolidated ('preciscen') texts of laws such as the Zakon o kreditnim institucijama, plus a 'dnevna azurnost' daily-update feed. Extremely useful as a low-friction change detector for CBCG instruments and as a cross-check that no gazette issue was missed; not authoritative and largely subscription-gated for full text.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Monitor the free 'dnevna azurnost' listing pages for gazette-issue contents only; do not scrape paywalled consolidated texts — resolve those to sluzbenilist.me or cbcg.me instead
queries_used: Sluzbeni list Crne Gore pretraga propisa sluzbenilist.me odluka Centralne banke

candidates.source_name: Katalog Propisa (katalogpropisa.me) — regulation update catalogue
candidates.why_relevant: Second commercial Montenegrin regulation catalogue exposing a 'pregled azuriranih propisa' (list of recently updated regulations). Serves as a redundant change-detection channel independent of PropisiNet, useful for catching amendments to CBCG bylaws quickly.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Light polling of the update-listing page only; treat as a tripwire, always confirm against cbcg.me / Sluzbeni list
queries_used: Sluzbeni list Crne Gore pretraga propisa sluzbenilist.me odluka Centralne banke

candidates.source_name: Investitor.me — Montenegrin financial trade press
candidates.why_relevant: Specialist Montenegrin finance/business outlet that covers CBCG regulatory moves substantively rather than as briefs — e.g. it reported the Zakon o kreditnim institucijama consultation and unpacked the crypto-asset scope, ownership-stake and ESG-supervision changes. Valuable for interpretation and for surfacing consultations whose primary announcement is easy to miss.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Keyword-filtered article monitoring (CBCG, kreditne institucije, platni promet, supervizija); store links and short extracts, not full text
queries_used: cbcg.me "javna rasprava" nacrt odluke Centralna banka Crne Gore

candidates.source_name: Kodex.me — Montenegrin business/legal news
candidates.why_relevant: Covers the closing phase of financial-sector consultations, including outcomes such as all comments being accepted on the Zakon o finansijskim konglomeratima amendments. Useful for the consultation-outcome stage that official portals report late or only as PDF annexes.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Keyword-filtered monitoring; corroborate every claim against the ministry or CBCG primary document
queries_used: eUprava Crna Gora e-participacija javne rasprave Ministarstvo finansija zakon o kreditnim institucijama nacrt

candidates.source_name: CBCG — LinkedIn company channel
candidates.why_relevant: First-party social amplification of CBCG announcements; occasionally posts consultation invitations and event notices ahead of, or instead of, a full website item. Low incremental value versus the saopstenja feed and hostile to automated collection.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Manual periodic review only; do not automate — LinkedIn ToS forbids scraping
queries_used: Centralna banka Crne Gore odluke propisi supervizija banaka
candidates.observed_blocker: LinkedIn company pages require authentication for full feed access and the platform ToS prohibits automated collection

negative_findings.description: Targeted local-language searching for a CBCG-hosted public-consultation section ('javne konsultacije', 'javna rasprava', 'nacrt odluke', 'rok za dostavljanje komentara') returned no dedicated consultations page under cbcg.me. The site navigation exposes Regulativa, Kljucne funkcije, Publikacije and Javnost rada, but no 'javne rasprave' node was observed in any navigation listing retrieved.
negative_findings.result_summary: Consultation on CBCG-originated primary legislation appears to be run by the Ministarstvo finansija on gov.me and the eUprava e-participacija portal instead. Whether CBCG consults publicly on its own secondary Odluke at all remains unresolved and is the single biggest open question for this cell.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A consultation watch pointed only at cbcg.me would produce systematic false negatives and miss every comment deadline on banking and payments legislation.

negative_findings.description: No RSS/Atom feed, open-data endpoint, or documented API was observed for the saopstenja, podzakonski akti, or register pages during navigation of cbcg.me. All retrieved content was rendered HTML with linked PDFs.
negative_findings.result_summary: Change detection for this cell will have to rely on scheduled HTML crawling with content hashing rather than subscribing to a feed. Not verified exhaustively — /rss and sitemap.xml paths were not probed in this pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Drives the collection architecture and cost for the densest source in the run; also means every deadline is discovered on crawl cadence, not push.

negative_findings.description: cbcg.me serves what appears to be the same content under many differing path prefixes observed in indexed results: /me/, /en/, /c/, /r/, /e/, /eng/, and even anomalous prefixes such as /live, /final_kursna.php/ and /luumyaydbzhv.html/. A direct fetch of https://www.cbcg.me/c/o-nama/regulativa/podzakonski-akti returned HTTP 404 while the /me/ equivalent returned content.
negative_findings.result_summary: Treated as a routing/canonicalisation quirk, not as a dead source. The 404 on the /c/ variant is a hypothesis about that specific path, not evidence the page is gone.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Naive crawlers will duplicate content, mis-record 404s as dead sources, and break stored URLs. Canonicalise every cbcg.me URL to the /me/ (or /en/) prefix and dedupe by path suffix and ?id= parameter before storage.

negative_findings.description: The podzakonski akti / Regulations landing pages expose their seven categories as in-page anchor fragments plus direct PDF links rather than as fully addressable per-instrument URLs; individual Odluke are not each given a stable HTML page.
negative_findings.result_summary: Per-instrument tracking must key on the PDF href and the 'Sl. list CG br. XX/YY' citation string, not on a per-decision page URL.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Determines the deduplication and versioning key for the entire regulatory corpus; without it, amendments to an existing Odluka are indistinguishable from new instruments.

negative_findings.description: sluzbenilist.me was located and a document-view URL pattern (/pregled-dokumenta-2/?id={GUID}) was observed, but whether full-text search and document download are free or subscription-gated was not established in this pass, and the site was not fetched directly.
negative_findings.result_summary: Access model recorded as unverified. Commercial mirrors (me.propisi.net, katalogpropisa.me) exist precisely because the official gazette is awkward to search, which is weak circumstantial evidence of friction.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The gazette is the legally authoritative text and the anchor for every effective date; a paywall would force reliance on CBCG-hosted PDFs as the working corpus.

negative_findings.description: English-language queries surfaced the /en/ mirror and Wikipedia but produced no source that local-language queries had not already found, and produced no consultation-related results at all. Local-language querying was strictly higher-yield for this cell.
negative_findings.result_summary: Both languages were searched as required; sr queries dominated on recall, en queries were useful only for the mirrored regulation index and for terminology alignment.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms that the collection design for Montenegro must be sr-first; an en-only pipeline would miss consultations and Council session outputs entirely.

coverage_gaps.description: It is not established whether the CBCG publishes drafts of its own secondary legislation (nacrti odluka) for public comment, or adopts them at Savjet sessions without prior consultation. Only ministry-run consultations on primary laws were confirmed.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Fetch https://www.cbcg.me/me/javnost-rada and the Savjet/organisational pages directly and enumerate all child nodes; probe for a 'javne rasprave'/'konsultacije' node; if absent, confirm via the Zakon o Centralnoj banci and the CBCG Statut whether any consultation obligation exists, and if still unresolved, use the pristup-informacijama channel to ask.

coverage_gaps.description: No page publishing supervisory enforcement actions, sanctions, fines, or mjere prema kreditnim institucijama was located. Only the 'restriktivne mjere' (international sanctions lists) node and the 'oduzeto odobrenje' payments list were observed, which are different things.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Search sr terms 'izrecene mjere', 'novcana kazna', 'prekrsajni nalog', 'oduzimanje dozvole', 'banka u stecaju' scoped to cbcg.me; also check the Izvjestaj o radu CBCG annexes, which typically aggregate the year's supervisory measures.

coverage_gaps.description: The cell scope names supervisory circulars, but no distinct circular/instruction channel (okruznice, uputstva, misljenja, cesto postavljana pitanja for supervised entities) was identified as separate from the formal Odluke corpus.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Search sr terms 'okruznica', 'uputstvo', 'instrukcija', 'misljenje CBCG', 'smjernice' on cbcg.me; the AML 'smjernice' found suggest guidance is filed inside functional sections rather than in one place, so enumerate per function.

coverage_gaps.description: Montenegro's banking/payments regulatory agenda is driven largely by EU accession Chapters 4 and 9. EU-side documents (European Commission Montenegro country report, screening and negotiating-chapter material, ECB/EBA convergence and technical-cooperation outputs) were not scouted in this pass and sit outside cbcg.me.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Flag to the run owner as a candidate for a separate coverage cell; these sources forecast CBCG regulatory obligations 12-24 months ahead of any domestic draft.

coverage_gaps.description: No mechanism was identified for retrieving superseded versions of CBCG Odluke; the site appears to present only the current corpus, and no CBCG-side archive node was observed.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Plan to seed history from the Wayback Machine for cbcg.me regulation pages and from Sluzbeni list issue archives, and to snapshot PDFs at first sight so the collection builds its own version history going forward.

coverage_gaps.description: Searching used Montenegrin/Serbian latinica only. Cyrillic variants and a small number of ijekavica/ekavica spelling differences (sprjecavanje vs sprecavanje, izvjestaj vs izvestaj) were not systematically exercised, and diacritics were dropped in some queries.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Re-run key queries with cyrillic transliteration and with full diacritics (c, c, z, s, dj) to test for missed items; note that Montenegrin official publication is latinica-dominant so expected yield is low but non-zero.

brief: The CBCG regulator channel is unusually well-structured and almost entirely first-party: a single site (cbcg.me, mirrored in English) carries the full legal corpus under /o-nama/regulativa (Zakoni, Statut, and Podzakonski akti in seven tracked categories), the functional supervisory hubs (kontrolna funkcija, platni promet, sanacija, AML/CFT, conduct protection, financial stability), the statutory licensing registers for banks, payment institutions, e-money institutions and payment systems, and the Savjet CBCG press-release feed that is in practice the earliest public signal of any regulatory change. The critical structural finding for this cell is that CBCG does not appear to host its own public-consultation section: draft primary legislation it authors — such as the Zakon o kreditnim institucijama amendments covering crypto-assets, ownership stakes and ESG in supervision — is consulted by the Ministarstvo finansija via gov.me and the eUprava e-participacija portal, so a consultations-and-deadlines watch must span three domains, with Sluzbeni list Crne Gore as the authoritative effective-date anchor and Skupstina as the adoption-date anchor. Collection will require scheduled HTML crawling with PDF hashing rather than feeds: no RSS or API was observed, individual Odluke exist only as PDFs behind in-page anchors keyed by their 'Sl. list CG br. XX/YY' citation, and cbcg.me serves duplicate content under many path prefixes so URLs must be canonicalised to /me/ or /en/ before storage. Local-language (sr) querying was decisively higher-yield than English for every consultation and Council-session item, and commercial aggregators (propisi.net, katalogpropisa.me) plus specialist trade press (investitor.me, kodex.me) are worth keeping as redundant, non-authoritative change tripwires.
